Plot Score Cards following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/cardsChart.R
wjp_cards.Rd

wjp_cards() draws a grid of rounded cards, one per row and column combination, colored on a sequential scale by their value, with the value printed in each card and, optionally, its difference from a reference card printed below it. Rows are labeled at the left and columns at the top.

Usage

wjp_cards(
  data,
  rows,
  cols,
  target,
  labels = NULL,
  deltas = NULL,
  ref = c("row", "col", "none"),
  limits = NULL,
  colors = c("#ECECF4", "#575796"),
  label_color = "auto",
  card_height = 48,
  card_gap = 6,
  radius = 3,
  label_width = 170,
  value_size = 16,
  delta_size = 9,
  card_width = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  label_gap = 12,
  label_size = 11,
  label_colour = "#1A1A1A",
  label_lineheight = 1.22,
  header_size = 11,
  header_fontface = "bold.italic",
  header_colour = NULL,
  header_gap = 7,
  header_lineheight = 1.2,
  value_fontface = "bold",
  value_color = "#1A1A1A",
  delta_fontface = "italic",
  delta_color = "#4B4B7A",
  min_shade = 0.12,
  dark_threshold = 0.55,
  row_order = NULL,
  col_order = NULL,
  margins = NULL,
  ptheme = WJP_theme()
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the data to plot.

rows

String. Column name of the variable with the row labels.

cols

String. Column name of the variable with the column labels.

target

String. Column name of the variable with the values (they set the colors and the default differences).

labels

String. Column name of the variable with the printed values. Default is NULL (rounded percentages of target).

deltas

String. Column name of the variable with the printed differences. Default is NULL (computed from target and ref).

ref

String. Reference cards: "row" (first row, default), "col" (first column), or "none".

limits

Numeric vector of length 2 with the range of the color scale. Default is NULL (range of the rounded values).

colors

Character vector of length 2 with the colors of the low and high ends of the scale. Default is c("#ECECF4", "#575796").

label_color

Color of the values and differences: "auto" (default: white on dark cards, value_color and delta_color otherwise) or one color.

card_height

Numeric. Height of a card, in points. Default is 48.

card_gap

Numeric. Gap between cards, in points. Default is 6.

radius

Numeric. Corner radius of the cards, in points. Default is 3.

label_width

Numeric. Width of the row label column, in points. Default is 170.

value_size

Numeric. Size of the values, in points. Default is 16.

delta_size

Numeric. Size of the differences, in points. Default is 9.

card_width

Numeric. Width of a card, in points. Default is NULL (120, or the width that fills width).

width

Numeric. Total width of the figure, in points; cards take the space left by the label column. Default is NULL.

label_gap

Numeric. Gap between the row labels and the cards, in points. Default is 12.

label_size

Numeric. Size of the row labels, in points. Default is 11.

label_colour

String. Color of the row labels. Default is "#1A1A1A".

label_lineheight

Numeric. Distance between the baselines of label lines, in multiples of the label size. Default is 1.22.

header_size

Numeric. Size of the column headers, in points. Default is 11.

header_fontface

String. Font face of the column headers. Default is "bold.italic". Weight faces such as "semibold.italic" are accepted (see wjp_fonts()).

header_colour

String. Color of the column headers. Default is NULL (colors[2]).

header_gap

Numeric. Distance from the baseline of the last header line to the cards, in points. Default is 7.

header_lineheight

Numeric. Distance between the baselines of header lines, in multiples of the header size. Default is 1.2.

value_fontface

String. Font face of the values. Default is "bold".

value_color

String. Color of the values on light cards. Default is "#1A1A1A".

delta_fontface

String. Font face of the differences. Default is "italic".

delta_color

String. Color of the differences on light cards. Default is "#4B4B7A".

min_shade

Numeric between 0 and 1. Shade of the lowest value. Default is 0.12.

dark_threshold

Numeric between 0 and 1. Shade from which texts turn white with label_color = "auto". Default is 0.55.

row_order, col_order

Character vectors with the order of the rows (top to bottom) and columns (left to right). Default is NULL (order of first appearance).

margins

Numeric vector of four margins (top, right, bottom, left), in points. Default is NULL (room for the headers on top, 4 points below).

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The function expects one row per card: the row label in rows, the column label in cols, and the value in target. Rows and columns are drawn in order of first appearance, or in the order given by row_order and col_order.

Reference and differences. With ref = "row", the cards of the first row are the references of their columns; with ref = "col", the cards of the first column are the references of their rows. Reference cards show their value centered; the other cards show the value and, below it, the difference from their reference: the deltas column as given or, when deltas is NULL, the difference between the rounded values in percentage points (e.g., "+16 points"). ref = "none" draws values only. A card with an empty or missing delta also shows its value centered.

Colors. The fill of each card mixes colors[1] and colors[2] in RGB space (see scale_fill_wjp_seq()) at min_shade + (1 - min_shade) * (value - limits[1]) / diff(limits). With label_color = "auto", texts on cards past dark_threshold are white.

Geometry in points. Cards are card_height points high, card_width points wide (or as wide as a figure of width points allows), and card_gap points apart, with corners of radius points. Row labels are wrapped to label_width - 4 points and right-aligned label_gap points before the cards; column headers are wrapped to the card width minus 8 points and their last line sits header_gap points above the cards. The chart has a definite size, so wjp_save() needs no width or height. Text widths are measured with systemfonts when it knows the font family (see wjp_fonts()), and estimated otherwise.

Examples

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Hardships by outcome of the problem (fictional data)
cards <- data.frame(
  hardship = rep(c("At least one hardship", "Health issues", "Economic issues"), each = 2),
  outcome  = rep(c("Fully resolved", "Not resolved"), 3),
  value    = c(46, 62, 30, 40, 26, 36)
)

wjp_cards(
  cards,
  rows   = "hardship",
  cols   = "outcome",
  target = "value",
  ref    = "col",
  width  = 468
)
